subject: Problems to define binary distribution in Stan

messages.author: 3d23175264b128d0
messages.subject: Problems to define binary distribution in Stan
parts:
Hi everyone.

I've tried to implement in Stan a hierarchical model in which the latent variable has p.d.f h(u/nu1,nu2) =  nu1 I(u=v2) + nu2 I(u=1) where nu1 and nu2 assume values between 0 and 1
I'm having problems to implement this distribution in Stan. The code I've wrote is below

data {
  int<lower=1> n;
  real<lower=0,upper=1> y;
  real b;
  real s;
  real l;
}

parameters {
  real Delta;          
  real mu;           
  real<lower=0> tau; 
  real<lower=0,upper=1> nu1;
  real<lower=0,upper=1> nu2;
  int<lower=0,upper=1> u_new[n];
  vector<lower=0>[n] h;
  real theta;
}

transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma2;          
  real del;           
  real gama; 
  vector<lower=0,upper=1>[n] u;
  del= Delta/sqrt(tau+square(Delta));
  sigma2=tau+square(Delta)*(1-square(b));
  gama= (b*pow(del,3)*l)/sqrt(pow((1-square(b*del)),3));
  for(i in 1:n){
    u[i]<- if_else(u_new[i]==0, nu2, u_new[i]);
  }
}

model {
  Delta ~ normal(0, 10);
  mu ~ normal(0, 10);
  tau ~ gamma(0.1, 0.1);
  nu1 ~ beta(1,1);
  nu2 ~ uniform(0,1);
  for(i in 1:n){
    u_new[i] ~ bernoulli(1-nu1);
    y[i] ~ normal(mu+(Delta/sqrt(u[i]))*(h[i] - b), sqrt(tau/u[i]));
    h[i] ~ normal(0,1);
  }
  
}


But I've got the following message:

SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

integer parameters or transformed parameters are not allowed;  found declared type int, parameter name=u_new
Problem with declaration.

ERROR at line 15

 13:      real<lower=0,upper=1> nu1;
 14:      real<lower=0,upper=1> nu2;
 15:      int<lower=0,upper=1> u_new[n];
                                       ^
 16:      vector<lower=0>[n] h;

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'scn' due to the above error.

Can anybody help me, please?

Thank you!!

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problems to define binary distribution in Stan
parts:
Stan does not allow discrete parameters.  To fit such a distribution
you’ll need to marginalize out u to give a latent mixture model.  See
the manual for more details.
